# s269 — Explain why to use slicer in docs/why-slicer.md

Neither the README nor `docs/` says why someone would use slicer. The README intro says what slicer is: roadmap and slice management, AI-friendly, JSON state in git, stdlib only. Nothing pairs the workflow problems people hit with the features that fix them. This slice adds `docs/why-slicer.md`, a one-screen page that does that, and links it from the README.

**Findings:** owner, 2026-10-14: README and docs never say why to use slicer; asked for a brief problem-to-feature page under docs, linked from the README · **Size:** S · **Tree:** docs

## Why

The owner asked for this on 2026-10-14: something brief that highlights the features and the workflow problems slicer smooths out. A reader deciding whether to adopt slicer currently has to piece that together from the command reference. One short page lets them judge quickly, and the README links send them there.

## Implement

1. Write the two tests and watch them go red.
2. Write `docs/why-slicer.md` with these parts:
   - an `# Why slicer` title;
   - a two- or three-sentence opening: planning in loose markdown works until several people or agents share it, and slicer keeps the plan as checked state in the repo;
   - 6 to 8 bullets, each a bold common problem followed by the slicer feature that fixes it, with a link to the doc that covers that feature. Cover these, and check each one against the code before writing it:
     - choosing the next task (`next --ready`, scores, dependencies);
     - two people or agents taking the same task (`start` claims across worktrees);
     - a roadmap drifting from the code (`check`, and `verify` against git history);
     - merge conflicts on tracking files from parallel branches (the merge drivers and `setup-git`);
     - agents needing a contract (`--json`, stable error codes, `ai instructions`);
     - vague specs (slice sections, and `next` withholding a slice with missing sections);
     - review (handoff → review → done, and the slice relay with its role matrix);
     - nothing to host (JSON in the repo, stdlib, no service or API key);
   - a short "When slicer is not for you" paragraph drawn from the non-goals in `slicer goals`, such as real-time collaboration and a hosted service.

   Keep it to about one screen. Match the plain, direct tone of `docs/getting-started.md`, wrapped at about 90 columns.
3. Add the README links: in the intro, "Why use it? See [Why slicer](docs/why-slicer.md)."; in `## Documentation`, first entry: "[Why slicer](docs/why-slicer.md) — the workflow problems slicer solves".
4. Add a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry under Added.
5. Mutation-check both tests: remove each README link in turn, then break one link in the page.
